framing.core_rule: Separate the polymer, residual monomer, additive, processing aid, contaminant, emitted chemical, and micro/nanoplastic particle; evidence for one entity and route does not transfer automatically to the others.
framing.population_rule: Separate workers, fence-line communities, consumers, pregnant people, infants, and patients because dose and route differ.
framing.causality_rule: Use causal language only for evidence that supports it. Biomonitoring and clinical associations identify concerns but do not prove that swallowing plastic caused the outcome.

micro_and_nanoplastics.finding: Microplastics and nanoplastics have been reported in foods and human samples, but current evidence and nonstandard analytical methods do not demonstrate that the levels detected in foods pose a human-health risk.
micro_and_nanoplastics.dashboard_text: People are exposed to plastic particles, but the health risk at measured food levels is not yet quantified; methods and dose-response evidence remain major gaps.
micro_and_nanoplastics.prohibited_text: All ingested microplastics are proven toxic at real-world doses.

micro_and_nanoplastics.finding: Polyethylene was detected in 58.4% and PVC in 12.1% of excised carotid plaques. Patients with detected particles had an adjusted hazard ratio of 4.53 (95% CI 2.00-10.27) for myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from any cause during follow-up.
micro_and_nanoplastics.dashboard_text: Plastic particles in carotid plaque were associated with later cardiovascular events in one selected surgical cohort; the study cannot identify the exposure source or prove causation.
micro_and_nanoplastics.prohibited_text: Ingested plastic causes a 4.53-fold cardiovascular risk in the general population.

pregnancy_vaccine_claim_audit.what_the_study_measured: Maternal serum perfluorinated compounds at pregnancy week 32 and child serum at age 5 in a prospective Faroese birth cohort; antibody concentrations after routine tetanus and diphtheria vaccination were measured at ages 5 and 7.
key_results: A twofold higher concentration of PFCs in the child at age 5 was associated in a structural-equation model with a 49.4% lower joint tetanus/diphtheria antibody concentration (95% CI 23.0%-66.7% lower).
Twofold higher PFOS or PFOA concentrations were associated with odds ratios of 2.38-4.20 for antibody concentrations below the study's protective threshold for some outcomes.
Some exposure-outcome associations were null, and this observational study did not test whether a mother ate a large quantity of microplastic particles.
pregnancy_vaccine_claim_audit.correct_dashboard_text: Prenatal and childhood exposure to certain PFAS was associated with reduced antibody responses to tetanus and diphtheria vaccines in a Faroese cohort. This is not evidence that ingested microplastic particles broadly caused vaccines to fail.
pregnancy_vaccine_claim_audit.prohibited_text: Mothers who ate many microplastics had babies whose vaccines did not take.
pregnancy_vaccine_claim_audit.why_plastics_are_relevant_but_distinct: Some PFAS have been used in polymer processing, fluorinated containers, and food-contact applications, but PFAS are chemicals, not synonymous with plastic particles or every plastic product.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: No blanket finding in the cited sources that intact polyethylene polymer is carcinogenic through ordinary consumer contact.
priority_hazards: microplastic and fragment exposure remains under study
additives and contaminants vary by formulation
certain fluorinated HDPE containers can form and leach PFAS
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Large volume, packaging leakage, persistence, fragmentation, and avoidable single-use applications.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: The PFAS finding applies to certain fluorinated containers, not all HDPE.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: No resin-wide human disease conclusion is supported here for ordinary consumer contact.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Highest modeled U.S. consumption among individual resins and extensive short-lived packaging use.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not infer toxicity from market volume alone.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: The cited evidence does not establish that ordinary PET package contact causes a specific disease.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: High-volume bottles, packaging, and textiles create capture and shedding priorities.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not transfer evidence about unrelated phthalate plasticizers to PET because of the shared word fragment.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: Vinyl chloride monomer is known to be a human carcinogen; that classification is not a quantitative risk estimate for ordinary contact with finished PVC.
priority_hazards: vinyl chloride occupational and fence-line exposure
phthalate and other additive exposure in flexible formulations
dioxin and furan formation under uncontrolled combustion
PVC particles observed in a clinical association study
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Prioritize monomer emissions, high-exposure flexible formulations, unnecessary products, and combustion controls.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Distinguish monomer, formulation additives, particles, installed product, and combustion.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: Styrene is reasonably anticipated to be a human carcinogen based on the NTP evaluation; this is principally a chemical and exposure-route finding, not proof that using a polystyrene cup causes cancer.
priority_hazards: styrene exposure in production and fabrication
food-contact migration depends on conditions and formulation
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Avoidable foam foodware and protective packaging are leakage-prone and difficult to recover.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Keep styrene hazard and finished-polystyrene exposure distinct.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: Isocyanates used to make PU are potent irritants and sensitizers and are a recognized cause of occupational asthma; cured PU has a different exposure profile.
priority_hazards: worker exposure to isocyanates during production, spraying, and curing
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Control reactive-chemical exposure and replace nonessential foam where performance is validated.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not apply uncured isocyanate hazard directly to every cured PU article.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: Acrylonitrile is reasonably anticipated to be a human carcinogen; that classification is relevant to ABS, SAN, and acrylonitrile-rich acrylic-fiber supply chains, not to methyl-methacrylate-based PMMA by name association.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Tight process controls, disclosure, and product-specific substitution for high-exposure uses.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not call finished ABS carcinogenic solely from the monomer classification, and do not transfer acrylonitrile evidence to PMMA.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: Bisphenol A is used in polycarbonate and epoxy systems. U.S. agencies publish differing risk framings and use restrictions; date and application must be shown.
priority_hazards: substitute bisphenols may be incompletely characterized
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Reduce exposure in food-contact, thermal-paper, and sensitive-life-stage applications where safer validated systems exist.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not hide current FDA and EPA positions or imply that every BPA-containing article produces the same exposure.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: This package has no basis for a resin-wide clinical toxicity conclusion.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Reduce shedding, extend textile and gear life, and improve retrieval and take-back.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not generalize one polyamide formulation to the whole family.

resin_and_chemistry_matrix.polymer_evidence: The polymer and the broad PFAS family are related in some supply chains but are not interchangeable toxicological entities.
priority_hazards: persistent PFAS used in processing or surface treatment
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.high_confidence_reason_to_act: Prevent PFAS releases and prioritize essential-use evaluation and disclosure.
resin_and_chemistry_matrix.guardrail: Do not call every fluoropolymer exposure equivalent to serum PFOS or PFOA exposure.

replacement_health_rule: The case for replacement is strongest where the use is unnecessary, exposure or release is credible, safer alternatives are validated, leakage is likely, and loss of performance does not create a larger health risk. Critical medical, food-preservation, electrical, and infrastructure uses require application-specific transition plans.
